ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $6.61 rider-initiated cancellation fee under NS-4; inform the rider of the NS-7 human review channel (30-day window, voucher form) if she wishes to contest it.
ruling.reasoning:
A plain text reading of the full chat (F7, F8, F9), the rider's complaint and the driver's written statement (F10) finds no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation; the only messages are a pickup query and an ETA reply [F7][F8][F9][F10][SAFE-1]. The driver's early statement that he was "still on the way" [F10] corroborates the GPS record and is not an allegation against the rider, so the safety screen returns none and no SAFE-1/SAFE-2 escalation is required, consistent with the trace's allowed outcomes [F1][F10][SAFE-2].

The cancellation was made by the rider, so NS-0 routes the fee through the rider-cancellation branch [F2][NS-0]. NS-4 makes the fee chargeable only when the rider cancels more than 3 minutes after matching: acceptance was 17:12:00 and cancellation 17:15:05 [F2], which is 185 seconds, i.e. more than the 180-second free window [F2][NS-4]. The record confirms the $6.61 cancellation fee was charged [F5], with no surge inflating it [F6], so under the trace the amount is correct and unaltered [F5][NS-4].

The driver's failure to reach the pickup is real: his closest approach was 1725 m, he never came within 200 m, no arrival was recorded, and he never pressed "I'm Here" [F1][F3][F4]. But those facts bear on the NS-1 branch, which only governs a driver-pressed no-show charge where the driver cancels: here no arrival confirmation exists [F4], so NS-1 and NS-2 are not engaged at all and cannot be used to refund a fee that was never charged on that basis [F3][F4][NS-1][NS-2]. The charge that actually exists is the rider-initiated cancellation fee [F5], whose only precondition under NS-4 is the three-minute threshold, which is satisfied [F2][NS-4].

Ryde publishes no rule entitling a rider to free cancellation because the driver has not yet arrived; the comparable rule is only informational and cannot be applied [F8][NS-0]. The driver's own message "Coming, about 5 min" at 17:13 [F8] shows he was still en route and the rider was informed before she cancelled, which supports the factual basis of the fee rather than defeating it [F2][F8][NS-4]. No profile fact is needed to decide the case: the driver's clean history [F15] and the rider's single prior dispute [F14] are noted but neither determines the outcome [F14][F15][NS-4].

The dispute was filed within the 30-day window and the complaint itself seeks a fee refund, so NS-7 is satisfied on timeliness; the remedy the rider retains is the Ryde human/voucher channel, not an automatic refund [F2][NS-7]. The evidence is complete for every element this ruling needs: the cancellation side, timing and fee are all recorded in the timeline and fare facts [F2][F5], and the chat record is complete with every message timestamped, so there is no G12-style hole in the record [F9][NS-4].

Conceded as fact: the driver never tapped 'I'm Here' and no automatic arrival was recorded [F4], but this merely removes NS-1/NS-2 from the case; it does not create a refund route for the $6.61 charged under NS-4 [F4][F5][NS-1][NS-2][NS-4].

NS-0 routes a rider cancellation to NS-4, and NS-4 makes the fee chargeable after 3 minutes of matching; the cancellation at 17:15:05 is 185 s after acceptance at 17:12:00, i.e. outside the free window, and NS-2 applies only to a driver cancelling for rider no-show [F2][F5][NS-0][NS-2][NS-4].

The messages are admitted, but 'Coming, about 5 min' and 'while I was still on the way' show only that the driver was en route, which is not an element of NS-4; the rider was informed of the ETA before cancelling [F8][F10][F2][NS-4].

Accepted as to quantum — $6.61 with a 1.0x surge [F5][F6] — but the quantum was never in dispute; the fee is correctly charged under NS-4, and any contest is a matter for the NS-7 review channel [F2][F5][NS-4][NS-7].
Accepted: the chat record is complete and fully timestamped [F9], which settles the timing element for NS-4; completeness confirms rather than displaces the three-minute breach [F2][F9][NS-4].

Profile facts are noted but never decide a case; the driver's clean history and the rider's single prior dispute are irrelevant to the NS-4 threshold and to RD-6, which concerns flagging only where a route dispute is upheld against the driver [F14][F15][RD-6].
